records.title: KV-LTM: Persistent Per-Session KV Caches as Long-Term Memory for Personal Assistants
records.claim: Storing each session's raw text plus its KV cache can serve as a long-term memory tier for personal assistants, trading storage for avoided re-prefill compute.

method_and_setup.method: A memory tier storing each session's raw text plus its KV cache under a fixed reader model, answering by restoring cached sessions and appending the question.
method_and_setup.setup: Analytic sizing across pinned BF16 full-attention (GQA) and latent-cached MLA configurations at a declared 30K-token/day scenario; an evaluation protocol on LongMemEval is specified but outcomes are not assumed.

results.measures: analytic storage per user-year at a declared 30K-token/day scenario
raw text for the same scenario

records.limits: Design and analytic sizing only; the evaluation protocol and real-cache replay outcomes are not assumed.
records.change_for_agents: Keep text as the memory of record and treat any KV cache as a droppable prefill accelerator with a retention budget.
records.why_it_matters_for_justin: Directly relevant to persistence across sessions for a personal assistant: text stays the record, the cache is only a prefill accelerator, but storage at 0.34-3.6 TB per user-year rules it out on a phone or a 64 GB Mac without a tight retention budget.

records.title: SkillBuffBench: Measuring What Agent Skills Contribute across Harnesses, Models, Skill Access Modes and Memory
records.claim: The benefit of agent Skills should be measured with automatic invocation from an installed library and with memory on, across harnesses and models, not with a hand-picked Skill and a blank slate.

method_and_setup.method: A paired benchmark treating Skill access as a three-level factor crossed with memory (off and on), four agent harnesses and multiple models, scored by deterministic verifiers with a paired task-level bootstrap.
method_and_setup.setup: Research tasks from domain experts in materials science and biology, with the Skills they use; cost, agent rounds and wall-clock time reported alongside the score.

records.limits: The evaluation is in progress; results will be added once the runs are complete.
records.change_for_agents: Evaluate skills under automatic invocation from a full installed library and with memory enabled, not only with a curated skill.
records.why_it_matters_for_justin: Skills are shipped by every major harness but the evidence assumes a hand-picked skill and a blank slate; this is the benchmark shape to copy when you test whether Mitamaton's installed skill library helps or hurts.

records.title: What Does an Agent Need? Bundle-Aware Agent Resource Composition
records.claim: Jointly selecting a backbone model and a tool-skill bundle per task beats scoring resources independently.

method_and_setup.method: Retrieval-Grounded Bundle-Aware Agent Generation: retrieve candidate resources and past configurations, recombine with a fine-tuned generator via constrained beam search, and rank bundles with a bundle-aware critic.
method_and_setup.setup: Reference recovery, offline execution with judged and native rewards, and online recommendation with real execution on AgentSelect-Exec with 5,060 executed configurations; SkillsBench.

results.measures: AgentSelect queries whose complete reference configuration is recovered within ten candidates
top-ranked agent's execution score with the proxy-trained critic
execution score with execution feedback

records.change_for_agents: Rank tool-and-skill bundles together with the model rather than scoring each resource independently.
records.why_it_matters_for_justin: Per-task selection of model plus tools and skills is the routing problem a multi-tool day-admin agent hits as the skill and MCP library grows; compare against simple retrieval before building a learned selector.

records.title: WebAgents: Unbundling Agent Creation, Hosting, and Execution for an Agent-Native Web
records.claim: Agent behavior can move across creators, hosts and runtimes via a signed package while execution authority stays in the user's runtime.

method_and_setup.method: A signed agent.pkg carrying portable workflows, skills, schemas and resource requirements, verified and bound at run time by an OpenClaw-based agent-native browser/runtime to user-controlled models, tools, permissions and budgets.
method_and_setup.setup: Three unrelated workflows run unchanged under local and API-backed models, plus a controlled suite of injected contract violations and matched benign controls.

results.measures: explicitly blocked in the controlled suite
accepted in the controlled suite
median automated pre-execution processing for all three packages

records.change_for_agents: Ship skills as signed packages that declare resource requirements and verify them before binding to the user's models and tools.
records.why_it_matters_for_justin: A signed, portable skill/workflow package that runs unchanged under local or API models is close to the identity-across-runtimes problem; useful reference for how to gate a skill before it runs on-device.

records.title: Can You Undo It? Reversibility Classes for AI Agent Actions
records.claim: Permission to call a tool does not establish whether a mistake can be undone, so tools should be classified into declared reversibility classes with prior-state capture.

method_and_setup.method: A declared five-level Reversibility Classes vocabulary with argument-sensitive rules, conservative defaults and a prior-state capture contract, implemented as a session guard.
method_and_setup.setup: Evidence-linked registry of 536 tools across 20 MCP servers; 2,158 recorded runs; controlled file, Git, SQLite and three-browser recovery experiments.

results.measures: runs where the session guard gates the associated action
attack-positive runs gated by a read/write proxy

results.value: nine approval points across 1,209 benign runs
results.measures: added approvals from the guard

records.limits: Does not establish registry-wide accuracy, reduced production harm or general recovery reliability; one AI-assisted reviewer is not independent agreement.
records.change_for_agents: Gate MCP tool calls by reversibility class and capture prior state before irreversible actions.
records.why_it_matters_for_justin: Directly usable as a permission model for MCP tools in a day-admin agent: classify by whether a mistake can be undone, not just read versus write, and capture prior state before irreversible calls.

records.title: EvoDisco: Strategy Discovery for Evolving Agent Memory
records.claim: Agent memory evolution is better framed as learned strategy discovery over semantic operators than as a fixed operator schedule.

method_and_setup.method: A learnable policy conditioned on memory state and recent task history selects and instantiates one of four operators (Abstract, Refine, Bridge, Reframe), trained with an inner retrieval-quality fitness and an outer strategic-efficacy fitness.
method_and_setup.setup: One-pass online plus frozen-transfer protocol on ALFWorld, WebShop and LifelongAgentBench (OS and DB), against MemP and MemRL.

results.measures: ALFWorld gain
ALFWorld gain

records.change_for_agents: Replace a fixed memory-consolidation schedule with selectable compress/split/link/reorganize operators chosen from memory state.
records.why_it_matters_for_justin: Gives a concrete operator set for compacting and reorganizing an agent's own memory instead of a fixed write schedule; worth comparing against whatever consolidation pass Mitamaton uses.

records.title: RegimeCouncil: Paired-Evidence Routing For Memory Conflict Governance In LLM Agents
records.claim: Neither a local nor a global memory-suppression scope is sufficient alone, and a lightweight router that arbitrates between them outperforms either.

method_and_setup.method: A paired-evidence router: a Local Advisor, a Global Advisor and a Meta Governor that follows local by default and switches to global only when pooled recent utility margin is strictly positive.
method_and_setup.setup: LongMemEval update streams, TempLAMA and TAQA with Qwen3-30B-A3B and GPT-4o.

results.measures: gain over the better fixed-scope policy on primary disagreement episodes
accuracy lost when any one of the three modules is removed

records.change_for_agents: Keep both local and global memory-suppression policies and switch between them based on recent with/without-memory outcomes.
records.why_it_matters_for_justin: Stale facts are the core failure of a long-lived personal memory; this is a no-retraining router that decides how far a bad-memory signal should spread.

records.title: Readie: Low-Latency Code Sandboxes for AI Agents
records.claim: A set of learned startup snapshots lets code sandboxes start quickly while covering most agent-generated code.

method_and_setup.method: Formulate snapshot construction as an optimization problem over a training workload and solve it with an approximation algorithm.
method_and_setup.setup: Planned on 15K public and LLM-synthesized scripts and compared with existing approaches at the same storage budget.

results.measures: size of the planning workload

records.change_for_agents: Pre-warm several small sandbox snapshots covering common package sets instead of one fat image.
records.why_it_matters_for_justin: Relevant if code execution is offloaded from the harness to a sandbox; shows startup, not the model, can dominate latency for short agent-generated scripts.

records.title: RAG in a Trenchcoat: When Minimal Memory Is Enough for Agentic Systems, and When It Isn't
records.claim: A minimal RAG memory matches heavier agentic-memory pipelines on standard benchmarks, so memory should be evaluated on what it enables an agent to do, not only on what it retrieves.

method_and_setup.method: BRIDGE: chained observation notes, hybrid BM25 with cosine retrieval and chronological rendering, plus five adversarial probes judged by a cross-vendor verification chain.
method_and_setup.setup: LongMemEval-S, BEAM, EverMemBench; 5 probes x 20 scenarios across four domains, three graders and three reader families.

results.measures: BRIDGE gain over the best memory baseline on EverMemBench at matched reader
BRIDGE prompt size

records.change_for_agents: Start with minimal hybrid retrieval memory and add extraction or graph layers only when an action-based probe shows they help.
records.why_it_matters_for_justin: A strong argument to start with minimal retrieval memory and evaluate on what memory enables the agent to do; also a warning against paying for extraction and graph layers you cannot show earn their cost.

records.title: Context Has a Price: Adding and Removing Context for LLM Coding Agents under Prefix Caching
records.claim: Adding or removing context for coding agents should be judged with separate prices for uncached input, cached input and output, because shorter prompts do not guarantee cheaper runs.

method_and_setup.method: A measurement study accounting separately for uncached input, cached input and output tokens across evidence-package and observation-removal interventions.
method_and_setup.setup: More than 20,000 runs of open models on SWE-bench Verified, SWE-bench and Loc-Bench.

results.measures: cost increase from retrieved code at a tenth-price cache
cost increase from removing old observations with a tenth-price cache
savings from removing old observations without a cache discount

records.change_for_agents: Evaluate context pruning and compaction with cache-aware token pricing and measure the extra steps the agent takes afterward.
records.why_it_matters_for_justin: Context trimming and compaction can raise your bill once the provider's prefix cache is priced in; test any history-pruning in the harness against cached-token prices, not raw token counts.

records.title: Multi-Agent Memory Inconsistency: Where Factual Conflicts Disappear in LLM Agents
records.claim: Delegating evidence collection to workers with separate contexts increases retrieval of conflicting claims but lowers conflict detection, because worker-to-lead handoffs lose the conflict.

method_and_setup.method: A benchmark and evidence-flow profiler built on controlled factual conflicts in Harvey LAB document-review tasks.
method_and_setup.setup: Pooled across three models with comparable generation spending; single-agent versus required delegation.

results.measures: retrieval of both conflicting claims with delegation versus single-agent
conflict detection with delegation
retrieved pairs for which workers report both claims

records.change_for_agents: Make worker-to-lead handoffs carry raw evidence and explicit conflicts instead of free-form summaries.
records.why_it_matters_for_justin: If a lead agent synthesizes from sub-agent reports, conflicting facts are lost at the handoff; require workers to pass raw evidence and conflicts, not summaries.

records.title: Harnesses That Improve Themselves: A Unifying Framework for Self-Improving Agent Harnesses
records.claim: Self-improving harnesses should update modular runtime components behind validation gates rather than rewrite the full harness.

method_and_setup.method: A four-component harness model with a four-stage loop that diagnoses failures, proposes code patches, validates candidates and deploys updates.
method_and_setup.setup: Experiments on SWE-bench Lite across models and repositories compared with prompt reflection and full-harness rewrites.

records.change_for_agents: Let an optimizer propose small patches to one harness module at a time and only deploy those that pass a validation gate.
records.why_it_matters_for_justin: Names the harness mechanisms worth adding (pre-stop verifiers, loop breakers, persistent memory) and argues for validation-gated modular patches rather than whole-harness rewrites.

records.title: LMLineage: Content Lineage and Context Governance for LLM Agents
records.claim: Attributing output to input spans lets an agent compact only the context that has stopped being used.

method_and_setup.method: Out-of-band sentence-to-input-span attribution with calibrated confidences, plus concept-drift micro compaction.
method_and_setup.setup: 71 gold annotated sentences from 10 Chinese web-QA cases and 90 turns of multi-turn sessions across gpt-4o-mini, qwen3.8-27b and deepseek-v4-flash.

results.measures: per-turn attribution on a single GPU
concept-drift detection

records.limits: Drift-detection recall is bounded by attribution accuracy.
records.change_for_agents: Track which source documents the agent still references and compact only unreferenced ones, keeping user instructions verbatim.
records.why_it_matters_for_justin: Surgical compaction of stale sources, with instructions preserved verbatim, is a better fit for a long-running assistant than waiting for the context limit and summarizing everything.

records.title: When Agent Skills Go Stale: Runtime Behavior and Selective Maintenance in Evolving Environments
records.claim: Reusing stale skill state after an environment change can hurt, and selectively maintaining skill state recovers the loss.

method_and_setup.method: Selective maintenance: replay checks from successful executions without additional model calls, verify conflicts with skill state, repair affected content, validate updates, and rebuild when local repair is insufficient.
method_and_setup.setup: Four task settings and two models, comparing skill reuse before and after environment changes with no description of the change supplied.

results.measures: performance drop from previously beneficial skills versus no skill
execution cost increase from stale skills versus no skill
task accuracy improvement from maintenance over reusing stale state
reduction in execution steps from maintenance

records.change_for_agents: Re-run recorded success checks against each cached skill and repair or rebuild skills whose checks now fail.
records.why_it_matters_for_justin: Cached skills go stale when apps, APIs or UIs change; a replay-check-repair loop without extra model calls is a cheap maintenance pattern for a skill library.

records.title: PACT: Plan-Action Consistency Training by Preserving Correct Plans and Repairing Actions in GUI Agents
records.claim: Separating credit for correct plans from erroneous actions improves GUI-agent task success on mobile and desktop.

method_and_setup.method: Plan-Action Consistency Training: reference-aligned plan protection masking negative policy-gradient contributions, plus plan-aligned action repair via a preference surrogate.
method_and_setup.setup: Compared with an outcome-only RL baseline on AndroidWorld, AndroidControl High and the full 369-task OSWorld benchmark.

results.measures: AndroidWorld task success
rule-based plan-action consistency on AndroidControl High
task success on the full 369-task OSWorld benchmark

records.change_for_agents: When training GUI agents with outcome RL, do not penalize the whole response when only the action token span is wrong.
records.why_it_matters_for_justin: Mobile GUI agents often plan correctly but emit the wrong action; relevant if you train or fine-tune an open GUI model for on-device iOS-adjacent tasks.

records.title: EvoSkill-S1: Evolving Reusable Skills with Genetic-Inspired Operators
records.claim: Evolving skills directly with genetic-style operators and evaluator-gated write-back improves reusable skill banks.

method_and_setup.method: An RL-driven skill evolver that selects parent skills from hard-negative failures and produces child skills via five operators, with Skill Bank Fusion and a Procedural Skill Interface.
method_and_setup.setup: Math and code benchmarks under Qwen and GPT-family solvers.

results.measures: relative gain over the initialized skill banks
largest relative improvement over the strongest external baseline without direct skill evolution

records.change_for_agents: Write evolved skill candidates back to the library only when an evaluator confirms the update helps.
records.why_it_matters_for_justin: A concrete mutation and write-back loop for a skill library; the gains are on math and code benchmarks, so check transfer to tool-use skills before adopting.

records.title: Remembered as Brief: Stored Preferences SilentlyRemove Decision-Critical Information
records.claim: Preferences stored in assistant memory, including ones planted by a summarised web page, silently remove decision-critical information from later answers.

method_and_setup.method: An Inspect benchmark where only the assistant's memory varies: the user states a belief, the model infers it from a remark, or a web page the user asked to summarise plants it.
method_and_setup.setup: 100 everyday decisions across 25 domains tested on five models.

results.measures: later answers that miss a critical item for Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite and DeepSeek V4 Pro after the planted preference
omissions that are silent under a stated brevity preference
value-dependent choices where the two models pick an option for the user, versus none with neutral memory

records.change_for_agents: Never write memory preferences derived from fetched content without confirmation, and list must-know points before applying a stored user profile.
records.why_it_matters_for_justin: A prompt-injection-into-memory path: a web page can plant a preference that later strips warnings from answers; treat memory writes sourced from fetched content as untrusted and list must-know points before applying the user profile.

records.title: Think Once, Act Fast: Cost-Effective Recursive Self-Improvement for Decision Model Harness
records.claim: LLM reasoning can be converted into a reusable harness that lets a fast low-latency model act well while System-2 calls decline over time.

method_and_setup.method: A System-1/System-2 framework where an asynchronous LLM develops a modular harness (procedures, state memory, world models) retrieved by contextual relevance and prior utility and revised from environmental feedback.
method_and_setup.setup: Three datasets compared with LLM agents.

records.change_for_agents: Distill repeated LLM reasoning into retrievable procedures and state that a small fast model can execute.
records.why_it_matters_for_justin: Amortizing an expensive model into a harness that a small fast model executes is the local-model pattern for a latency-bound on-device agent.

records.title: SEAM: Computer-Use Agents Know the Harm Between Screens, and Commit It Anyway
records.claim: Computer-use agents recognise cross-screen compositional harm when asked but still commit it, because safety recognition does not reliably translate into safe execution.

method_and_setup.method: A benchmark of cross-screen compositional harm with minimal-pair variants scored from the server log rather than by an LLM judge.
method_and_setup.setup: 600 multi-step, cross-application OSWorld tasks; open-weight, flagship and proprietary agents.

results.measures: runs in which general-purpose open-weight and flagship agents carry out the harm
multi-step cross-application OSWorld tasks

records.change_for_agents: Run safety checks over the combined facts from multiple screens, and place constraints in the user instruction rather than on screen.
records.why_it_matters_for_justin: Per-screen and per-instruction guards are not enough for a computer-use agent; put checks over the accumulated cross-screen state, and state constraints in the user's instruction channel.

records.title: Runtime Verification of Multiple Natural Language Criteria for Agent Governance
records.claim: A single parallel verifier can check an agent's output against a large set of natural-language criteria and report which are satisfied, violated or inapplicable.

method_and_setup.method: A tree-attention verifier encoding shared context and target text and scoring N criteria in parallel, pretrained on CriteriaBank.
method_and_setup.setup: Synthetic governance benchmark and DynaBench multi-criterion benchmark; latency measured on a single H100.

results.measures: evaluation time for 1,000 criteria against a 4K-token context on a single H100
memory for VFM-4B in that setting
(context, target, criterion, verdict) tuples in CriteriaBank

records.change_for_agents: Score all governance criteria in one parallel verifier pass and escalate only the violated ones to a larger judge.
records.why_it_matters_for_justin: A small local verifier that checks many policy rules per output cheaply is a fit for runtime guards; at 4B parameters it is within reach of a 64 GB unified-memory machine, though the speed is reported on an H100.

records.title: Agent Trust Infrastructure (ATI): A Federated Identity, Trust, Attestation, and Accountability Architecture for Cross-Organization Autonomous AI Agents
records.claim: Cross-organization agents need federated identity, attestation of model, tool and system-prompt configuration, and authorization enforced outside the agent framework.

method_and_setup.method: An external enforcement layer built on PKI, Zero Trust Architecture and remote attestation using IETF WIMSE workload tokens and Entity Attestation Tokens.
method_and_setup.setup: Simulated federation of eight organizations using six agent frameworks with five-agent teams; 14 attack scenarios and six benign tasks across five models, judged by a panel of judge models.

results.measures: attack containment with all enforcement mechanisms enabled
enforcement overhead per request

records.change_for_agents: Verify an agent's certificate and approved model, tool and prompt configuration before executing its requests.
records.why_it_matters_for_justin: Identity and attestation across runtimes and organizations; relevant if your agents ever call other parties' agents or MCP servers, though the evaluation is simulated.

records.title: JET: Just-Enough Exploration Tuning for Efficient Tool-Calling Agents in Repository-Level Question Answering
records.claim: LLM agents keep calling tools after they have enough information, and fine-tuning on truncated trajectories with a rationale reduces this.

method_and_setup.method: Just-Enough Exploration Tuning: truncate each training trajectory where information becomes sufficient, insert an explaining rationale, and fine-tune with a higher loss weight on the rationale.
method_and_setup.setup: Two repository-level QA benchmarks with two open-weight 8B models.

results.measures: reduction in tool calls on self-generated trajectories
fewer tool calls than SFT on expert trajectories

records.change_for_agents: Train or prompt agents with explicit 'enough information, answer now' rationales.
records.why_it_matters_for_justin: Over-exploration burns tokens in tool-heavy agents; a stopping signal trained into a small local model is a cheap lever.

records.title: Evolution Under Fire: Evolving Agent Safety Harnesses with Adaptive Injection Stressors
records.claim: Safety harnesses evolved against adaptive injection attacks reduce attack success far below static defenses while retaining utility.

method_and_setup.method: Utility-constrained, Pareto-scheduled tree search that evolves executable safety harnesses from execution evidence, alternating with adaptive stressor evolution.
method_and_setup.setup: AgentDyn with GPT-4o-mini; Agent-SafetyBench with Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct; transfer to Qwen3.5-35B-A3B.

results.measures: attack success on AgentDyn with GPT-4o-mini
attack success on Agent-SafetyBench with Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct
attack success after transfer to Qwen3.5-35B-A3B

records.change_for_agents: Red-team your injection guard with adaptive attacks and iterate the guard on the failures.
records.why_it_matters_for_justin: Prompt injection through email and web content is the main risk for a personal agent; evolving the guard harness against adaptive attacks beats static hand-designed defenses in these tests.

records.title: CrossEnv: Synthesizing Verifiable Cross-Environment Tasks for Long-Horizon Agent Training
records.claim: Training on synthesized cross-environment tasks with a curriculum improves long-horizon tool-use agents with fewer examples.

method_and_setup.method: An entity-tool graph links environments and aligns task-specific data to synthesize executable, verifiable cross-environment tasks, with a CrossEnv-Curriculum.
method_and_setup.setup: Evaluated across four external benchmarks.

records.change_for_agents: Build test tasks where an action in one service depends on information from another.
records.why_it_matters_for_justin: Day-admin work crosses calendar, mail and files; this is a recipe for training or testing tool-using models on dependencies between services.

records.title: Done, But Still Working: Anytime Evaluation of When Coding Agents Should Stop
records.claim: Coding agents often continue after their own tests pass, and a simple stop rule can save cost but with uncertain quality preservation.

method_and_setup.method: Anytime evaluation: replay recorded runs, score intermediate patches with hidden tests and measure cost at each step.
method_and_setup.setup: About 6,000 runs of eight open models in two scaffolds on SWE-bench Verified.

results.measures: hindsight saving available at passing self-tests
savings from a rule that stops after the same patch passes twice in a preregistered replication
savings from fine-tuning agents to imitate the rule

records.limits: The preregistered quality test does not establish non-inferiority; quality preservation remains uncertain.
records.change_for_agents: Add a stop rule that ends a run after the same patch passes its tests twice, and monitor quality.
records.why_it_matters_for_justin: Agents keep working after their tests pass; a cheap stop rule can cut spend but quality preservation is not established, so gate it behind your own regression checks.

records.title: Fine-Tuning Gemma 4 Edge Models for MATLAB Signal-Processing Code with SFT and QLoRA on a Laptop iGPU
records.claim: Small Gemma 4 edge models can be fine-tuned on a laptop iGPU to fix systematic signal-processing code errors.

method_and_setup.method: SFT with LoRA and QLoRA on Gemma 4 E2B and E4B, deployed as int8 models with adapters through OpenVINO.
method_and_setup.setup: 66 checked examples covering 11 MATLAB subtasks, held-out variants scored by deterministic checkers.

results.measures: E2B pass rate with LoRA
E4B pass rate with QLoRA
generation speed cost of the adapter at run time

records.change_for_agents: Fine-tune a small edge model with a small checked dataset and deterministic checkers rather than relying on prompts.
records.why_it_matters_for_justin: Shows small domain adapters on edge-sized open models are trainable on consumer hardware; the 64 GB unified-memory machine has far more headroom than this iGPU setup, but the task here is MATLAB DSP code, not agents.

records.title: Consistency Is Not Correction: Separating Confidence, Abstention, and Recovery in LLM Agents
records.claim: A confidence signal that ranks answers well does not by itself correct them, and the binding constraint on this literature is measurement resolution.

method_and_setup.method: An exact decomposition of correction utility into gated recoveries minus gated harms, which bounds whether a paired comparison can succeed before it is run.
method_and_setup.setup: Two model scales; a small-model suite and a controlled 840-episode study including 60 GSM8K decisions.

results.measures: within-policy AUROC of the perturbation-agreement verifier
call count relative to single-sample decoding
size of the controlled study

records.change_for_agents: Compute the maximum discordant pairs a gate can produce before running a controller comparison.
records.why_it_matters_for_justin: Before adding a resample or escalate gate to an agent, check whether the experiment can show a gain at all; a high AUROC gate may change nothing at several times the cost.

records.title: FCP: Formal Context Protocol for Verifying LLM-Generated Artifacts
records.claim: Passing AI-written tests is weak evidence, and checking artifacts against a formal reading of the request catches violations that the tests accept.

method_and_setup.method: A protocol separating conformance (decided by model checkers and SMT solvers) from fidelity (refutable by a concrete witness) with eight mechanical checks for false certification.
method_and_setup.setup: Four hardware designs and ten code tasks with code from three language models.

results.measures: violated requirements certified by trusting AI-written assertions on four hardware designs
certified by trusting the tests on ten code tasks
violations certified by FCP on the same tasks

records.change_for_agents: Verify generated artifacts against the original request, not only against tests the same model wrote.
records.why_it_matters_for_justin: When an agent writes both the code and its tests, a pass is weak evidence; checking against the request is a pattern for verifying agent output.

records.title: Agent Trajectories as Evidence for Software Quality Assurance
records.claim: Agent trajectories can serve as evidence for targeted software quality assurance beyond final code and passing tests.

method_and_setup.method: A proposal to analyze observable agent trajectories together with software and agent specifications and AI-generated artifacts.

records.limits: Trajectories alone do not establish that decisions are justified, outcomes acceptable, or corrective changes effective.
records.change_for_agents: Log and review agent decision trajectories and flag consequential decisions for human review.
records.why_it_matters_for_justin: Keeping and reviewing the trajectory of a coding agent, not just its diff, is cheap to adopt for review; the paper itself offers no evidence yet.

records.title: Do LLM Agents Still Need to Be Told How to Self-Improve?
records.claim: Sufficiently capable frozen LLM agents can construct their own self-learning algorithm over text documents, and the resulting artifacts transfer.

method_and_setup.method: A frozen LLM agent with a compute budget and tools to collect experience and update text documents, free to experiment without an imposed loop.
method_and_setup.setup: Gameplay testbed with transfer evaluated on external benchmarks across game horizons, mechanics and 3D navigation.

records.change_for_agents: Give agents tools to write and revise their own text notes under a compute budget and measure transfer.
records.why_it_matters_for_justin: Context-document self-improvement without weight updates matches a memory-file design; evidence is from gameplay, so treat it as directional.

records.title: Mind the Gap: A Deployed Multi-Agent System for Documentation Maintenance
records.claim: A multi-agent triage system can turn support-ticket signals into documentation fixes that measurably improve later agent answers.

method_and_setup.method: A multi-agent system built around a triage agent, TriAgent, that extracts explicit and implicit signals and repairs documentation drift after human review.
method_and_setup.setup: 43 days of shadow-mode operation; a panel of LLM judges from independent model families and a blinded human audit.

results.measures: triaged over 43 days of shadow-mode operation
surfaced in the documentation
TriAgent's verifiable assertions that were correct (245 of 302)
blinded judges preferring the post-repair answer over the pre-repair answer

records.change_for_agents: Route resolved support tickets into a gap list that triggers reviewed documentation fixes.
records.why_it_matters_for_justin: A production example of agents consuming and repairing the docs other agents rely on; relevant to keeping a skill or memory knowledge base in sync with reality.
